note: Adjudicated variants: three of punctuation and eight of orthography — seven the house i/j rule, one (Genetrícis/Genitrícis) a genuine spelling divergence where both spellings are real words of the same recension and the edition rules which it prints. Substantive text agrees across all three witnesses with zero further divergence.

adjudicated.ruling: Both spellings are real: genetrix is the older form, genitrix the one that spread later, and the dictionaries head both. The typical edition prints Genetrícis throughout the Canon and its seasonal variants, and witness do follows it, so the edition prints that and records the hand missal's reading here rather than silently correcting a page that is not wrong. Whitaker's Words carries only genetrix; Collatinus carries both.

The j-form against this edition's i-form, by the house rule in ORTHOGRAPHY.md. This edition prints i because the books it edits do: the 1962 typical edition sets Iesu, Ioánnem, iube and maiestátis throughout, and so does the Mszał Rzymski of the Tyniec Benedictines (Pallottinum, Poznań 1963), which is the book a Polish reader is most likely to hold. The mid-century hand missals print j; neither spelling is a different word, and the apparatus records theirs.
